payload.baseline:
THE WINNER'S MATRICES, consolidated as the architecture. Nothing redrawn - X3's allocation and element DSM ARE the baseline. SEVEN ELEMENTS, each described black-box: what it takes, what it gives, what it may never do.

E1 THE SEARCH FACADE (K1/F1, F3, F4, F5, F6). TAKES: a pattern, an optional scope (working tree, a ref, or a declared root), filters, and caps. GIVES: match locations as typed records - source, path, line - never text to be scraped. NEVER: returns context (that is E2's job, per se.adr-locate-and-read-are-separate); exceeds its caps; searches outside the scope it was given. Realized over git grep -z; untracked files included by default for tree scopes.

E2 THE RANGE READER (K1/F2). TAKES: a path plus an optional range, or a path plus a ref. GIVES: exactly that range, with the total extent reported. NEVER: silently truncates - an oversize request without a range is REFUSED with the size and a remedy.

E3 THE HONEST ANSWER LAYER (K2/F7, F8, F9). TAKES: every inbound tool call, before dispatch. GIVES: either a validated call passed through, or a typed refusal naming what was expected, what arrived, and the executable remedy. NEVER: coerces a missing required argument into a value. DELIBERATELY ABOVE E1 AND E2 rather than inside them, so refusal semantics cannot vary per provider - which is exactly how a missing argument once became a confident search for the literal word 'undefined'.

E4 THE FILE WRITER (K3/F10-F13). TAKES: one or many edits, each with its own CAS guard. GIVES: an atomic application, or nothing at all with the failing edit named. NEVER: applies a partial batch; permits another lane to write the product unrecorded.

E5 THE PACKET BUILDER (K4/F14-F16). TAKES: a machine state. GIVES: the step's instruction plus every rule whose selector matches, resolved to content, with the guidance volume reported. NEVER: hands over a pointer the agent must chase, nor a rule set whose size is invisible.

E6 THE LINT REGISTRY (K5/F17-F21). TAKES: a gate and its declared check ids. GIVES: per check, pass with its fact, fail with the fact that did not hold, or defer. NEVER: parks; never judges intent; never returns a verdict the evidence cannot show.

E7 THE RECORD KEEPER (K6/F22-F25, F28) and E8 THE SETTINGS LANE (K6/F26-F27). E7 TAKES: a successful close, or a call to be logged. GIVES: a grant carrying the evidence commit hash, an annotated tag, a deleted branch, and a log line naming what was consulted. NEVER: pushes, force-pushes or rewrites history. E8 TAKES: a config read or write against the machine-local dir. GIVES: values with secrets masked, or a validation failure naming the field. NEVER: writes inside the repository; never returns a credential.

THE TEAR I FLAGGED AT PARTITIONING WAS TAKEN: K6 split into E7 (the record) and E8 (settings). They clustered only by weak coupling to everything, and the winner's allocation separates them because they share no data, no lifecycle and no failure mode - E8 is machine-local and uncommitted, E7 is the committed record itself.

METRICS: 8 elements, 7 declared interfaces, cluster count 6 against 28 functions. The K4-K5 contract edge that the partitioning named as load-bearing survives as I5 below, which was the constraint any candidate had to satisfy.
payload.allocation_exact:
EVERY FUNCTION ALLOCATED EXACTLY ONCE - the column property holds, and I checked it as a count rather than by reading down the list feeling satisfied.

E1: F1, F3, F4, F5, F6 (5). E2: F2 (1). E3: F7, F8, F9 (3). E4: F10, F11, F12, F13 (4). E5: F14, F15, F16 (3). E6: F17, F18, F19, F20, F21 (5). E7: F22, F23, F24, F25, F28 (5). E8: F26, F27 (2). TOTAL 28, matching the 28 functions derived at M3. No function appears twice; none is unallocated.

THE ONE THAT COULD HAVE BEEN DOUBLE-ALLOCATED, named because a clean count hides the judgement: F9 REPORT INCOMPLETENESS. An oversize read is refused by E2, which knows the size - so F9 could sit there. It sits in E3 instead, with the other honesty functions, because incompleteness is a property of an ANSWER rather than of a reader: search results are also capped (E1/F5), and if each provider reported its own incompleteness we would grow two dialects of 'there is more'. One place, one shape.

F28 RECORD-WHAT-WAS-CONSULTED sits in E7 rather than in E1/E2, for the same reason inverted: logging is a property of the RECORD, not of the reader, and putting it with the readers would mean two log shapes and a guarantee they drift.
payload.interfaces_both_ends:
SEVEN INTERFACES, each declared at both ends. The symmetry property holds; where it does not have to hold, that is stated rather than left as an apparent gap.

I1 E3 -> E1/E2/E4/E8 (validated call). Declared by E3 as 'a call matching the declared schema'; declared by each receiver as 'arguments are already validated - do not re-check, do not coerce'. SYMMETRIC.
I2 E1 -> caller (match locations). E1 gives typed records; the caller expects source, path, line and nothing more. SYMMETRIC.
I3 E1 -> git; I4 E2 -> git/filesystem. Argv in, NUL-separated fields or bytes out, exit code. Declared at our end as the parse contract; the far end is external and cannot declare anything - ASYMMETRIC BY NATURE, and named so: this is the boundary where a git version change would bite, and the only defence is that we own the arguments and the parsing.
I5 E5 <-> E6 (THE LOAD-BEARING ONE). A rule supplied to the agent and a rule enforced by a lint must be the SAME rule. Declared at both ends as a shared selector vocabulary: E5 selects rules by it, E6 keys checks by it. SYMMETRIC, and deliberately so - the partitioning named this edge as the constraint any candidate had to satisfy, and every surviving candidate did.
I6 E6 -> E7 (verdicts into the record). E6 gives per-check verdicts with their facts; E7 stores them in their own block, distinguishable from prose. SYMMETRIC.
I7 E4 -> E7 (a write becomes a record). Declared both ends: every applied edit is logged with its guard.

NO ELEMENT REACHES INSIDE ANOTHER. E6's lints read material through E1/E2 like any other caller rather than touching the filesystem directly - which keeps caps, containment and logging applying to lints too, and means a lint cannot quietly become a second reader with its own rules.

ONE HONEST WEAKNESS in the interface set: I3 and I4 both cross to git, and neither can be declared from the far side. If git's output shape changes, two interfaces move at once. That is the price of the winning candidate, it was visible in the scoring as C4's residual risk, and the mitigation is the M5 spike on NUL-parsing robustness rather than a design change.
